correctness.rationale: The Desargues graph is the 30-edge bipartite inclusion graph on 2- and 3-subsets of [5], and its independence complex is flag. A minimal-support nonzero H5 class needs at least 2·5+2=12 vertices; an equality support must be an octahedral S5 from a six-edge induced matching. An independent enumeration yielded induced matching counts [30,255,700,615,42,5,0] in sizes 1..7; the five six-edge matchings are the M_i obtained by fixing the omitted element i. Their signed 64-term sphere cycles are genuine 5-cycles. The integral ranks of ∂5,∂6,∂7 are forced to 932,383,97 by mod-101 lower bounds and the rank 388 primitive lattice L=im∂6+ΣZz_i; its exact 388×388 minor has determinant −1. I independently regenerated the 388-row and 388-column minor directly from the actual certificate indices and performed 388 exact integer unit pivots, obtaining −1. Thus L=ker∂5 as saturated equal-rank lattices and H5=Z^5 with the five specified integral generators. The S5 action exactly permutes the matching spheres, and complementation reverses all six chosen edges with net −1, giving Z[X]_perm⊗sgn_C2. The known H4=Z and nonequivariant homotopy type are not claimed new.
residual_risks: Finite independent checks do not prove the all-parameter claims; analytic arguments or exhaustive certificates are required.

value.rationale: Minimum-support cycles and their integral permutation-with-sign module are natural geometric/topological invariants for this symmetric named graph. A primitive integral basis is strictly stronger than a rank-five rational homology assertion, and the full S5×C2 action is useful for equivariant topology.
